plan.topic: Holiday drinks on Foundayo (orforglipron): what the US label covers, and why fluids and pacing matter
plan.angle: Sentence 1: 'Holiday drinks on Foundayo? Here's what the label does and doesn't say.' Then: 'The Foundayo label doesn't specifically address alcohol.' 'Nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are common.' 'The label says losing fluids from them may cause kidney problems.' Caveat: 'Your risk of low blood sugar may be higher if you also use insulin or a sulfonylurea.' Two untagged tips: 'Sip water alongside, unless you've been told to limit fluids.' 'Skipping the drink is fine too.' Then 'We can't give you a safe amount, so ask your prescriber.', the Foundayo emergency card ('severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting … right away'), the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop. Watch-next: ssb7Zcs3KSY.

plan.why: Foundayo paired with a practical searched question is our second-proven Shorts format (food rules 1,062, nausea 853), and holiday parties are starting. | fact-check: Confirmed in the Foundayo PI and Medication Guide at uspl.lilly.com/foundayo/foundayo.html (Revised: 7/2026): neither mentions alcohol, so 'the Foundayo label doesn't specifically address alcohol' is fine. Re-check the full PDF before scripting. Confirmed Medication Guide wording: 'Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting may cause a loss of fluids (dehydration) which may cause kidney problems.' The angle's caveat is too strong. The guide says low blood sugar risk 'may be higher if you use FOUNDAYO with medicines that can cause low blood sugar, such as an insulin or sulfonylurea', not 'is higher'. Don't claim that alcohol interacts with Foundayo or raises pancreatitis risk, because the label doesn't say so. Don't suggest any 'safe' number of drinks. The holiday is the setting, not the cause.

package.title: Foundayo (Orforglipron): Holiday Drinks, What the Label Says #shorts
package.description:
Foundayo's (orforglipron) US label does not specifically address alcohol. It does say nausea, vomiting and diarrhea may cause fluid loss, which may cause kidney problems, and that low blood sugar risk may be higher if you use Foundayo with insulin or a sulfonylurea. We cannot give you a safe amount, so ask your prescriber.

Stop taking Foundayo and call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area (abdomen) that will not go away, with or without nausea or vomiting. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
#Orforglipron
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every claim against the Foundayo label on Lilly's site (uspl.lilly.com/foundayo), which has both the full Prescribing Information and the Medication Guide. Everything holds up:
- The hook is correct: neither document mentions alcohol.
- The dehydration and kidney sentence in s2 matches the Medication Guide word for word.
- The low blood sugar line in s3 matches the guide and keeps "may be higher" and "insulin or sulfonylurea".
- The emergency sign in s6 matches the guide's wording, including "healthcare provider", "stomach area (abdomen)" and "with or without nausea or vomiting". Each card ends on a period or reads as one unbroken sentence.
- The don't-stop line uses "that emergency sign" because only one sign is named, and it is two cards.
- The source dates match the documents: Medication Guide issued 07/2026, Prescribing Information revised 7/2026.
- The s4 tips carry the fluid-limit caveat and, like the s5, s7 and s8 lines, have no source tag.
- The spoken word count (157) is inside the standard arm.

There is one small wording fix, in s2.

issues.claim: Nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are common, and the label says they may cause fluid loss
issues.problem: The video is about holiday drinks, but this sentence doesn't say what the symptoms are common with. A viewer could take nausea, vomiting and diarrhea as effects of alcohol that the label lists. The label lists them as common side effects of Foundayo and says nothing about alcohol.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Nausea, vomiting and diarrhea are common Foundayo side effects, and the label says they may cause fluid loss, which may cause kidney problems." This adds 2 words, so the total becomes 159, still within 160.
